answer: The protocol's quill of quadratic staking forces each Sybil node to lock collateral scaling as the square of its stake, so marginal capital cost rises super‑linearly. A slashing rule that burns a fixed fraction of the locked pool compounds this, requiring an ocean of forfeited value to overturn consensus. Since protocol revenue caps extractable gain, the attack expense exceeds any possible reward, rendering the prior incentive design a relic.
